title: Deaf ambulance driver’s proposed accommodation would’ve posed undue hardship, 1st Circuit affirms
summary: Technology connecting the plaintiff to an American Sign Language interpreter posed safety risks because it could have taken his eyes off of the road, the court said.

title: Meta’s AI-based layoffs allegedly targeted workers who had taken protected leave
summary: The company used “a constellation of internal artificial-intelligence systems” to determine who would be included in its 10% reduction in force, per a lawsuit.

title: In 2026, EEOC solidifies its lockstep with Trump’s anti-DEI agenda
summary: This year, the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission has been prolific in its agenda-setting and enforcement plans regarding diversity, equity and inclusion at work.

title: HR professionals can’t rely totally on AI tools to evaluate employees
summary: While top artificial intelligence models were adept at navigating tasks with clear answers, they weren’t able to effectively interpret nuance, per a report.

title: Starbucks rolls out quarterly bonuses for high-performing workers
summary: The latest perks could help the chain attract and retain workers needed to sustain its turnaround drive.

title: Fair chance hiring better received by applicants when a moral case is made, study finds
summary: Applicants often assign negative stereotypes to policies meant to expand opportunities to people with criminal histories, according to research published in the Journal of Management.

title: 10th Circuit revives Walmart worker’s charge of anti-gay hostile work environment
summary: Viewing the claim in the light most favorable to the worker means “interpreting plausibly homophobic comments as homophobic,” the court said.

title: New York Times accuses EEOC of retaliation in counterclaim
summary: “Everything about the Commission’s handling of this matter ... has been marked by irregularities,” the Times said in a court document.

title: Which company offers interns $8,600 per week?
summary: Competition for talent continues to heat up as companies face a skills mismatch driven by AI adoption.

title: Latest workforce development funds target specific industries — like nuclear energy and AI
summary: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation and the U.S. Department of Labor separately announced grants and funding designed to target critical occupations.
